title: Getting Started Running Without Aches and Pains (Jeff Galloway beginner run-walk schedule)
population: General adult beginners; author's own schedule, no outcome data
findings: 3 run days a week (Tue, Thu, Sat or Sun), with Mon off or gentle walking.

Weeks 1-2 run 5 s / walk 55 s inside a walk-run-walk session: Week 1 Tue walk 10, run-walk 10, walk 10 min; Thu 9 / 12 / 9; Sat or Sun 15 / 14 / 10. Week 2 Tue 7 / 16 / 7; Thu 6 / 18 / 6; Sat or Sun 15 / 20 / 15.
Weeks 3-4: Tue and Thu use 10 s run / 50 s walk with 10-18 min run-walk blocks; the long day stays at 5 s / 55 s and reaches 25 min (week 3) then 30 min (week 4) of run-walk.
Page: 'Many new runners stay at the level of week 4 for a month or indefinitely'; others use 15/45 for weeks 5-6, 20/40 for weeks 7-8 and 30/30 for weeks 9-10.
The page claims 'almost a zero rate of injury' among those who gradually increase this way (author's claim, no data on the page).
limitations: Author's own page, convention (D), no outcome data; the injury claim is unsupported; undated, so the year is the retrieval year.
implications: Public practice has a much lower floor than C25K: 5 s of running per minute at the start (about 50 s of running in a 10 min block), so the true novice floor can be far below 8 min of running.
Support for allowing a runner to stay at one level for a month or longer (hold rule) before ramping.

verification.notes: Re-fetched the page this session and read the week 1-4 schedule and the paragraph on weeks 5-10. Block lengths, run/walk ratios, the stay-at-week-4 quote and the injury claim match. No publication date found in page metadata. Clarified that the run-walk figures are run/walk ratios inside a block, not minutes of running. Practice source (programme, coaching or clinical page): a published convention, not evidence; grade D.
